answer: An agent marketplace selling prism optics, zenith sensors, and yarrow seeds requires each active identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can bid. A bond can back only one identity at a time, so creating 10,000 eligible agents ties up $1 million; generating more keys adds no bidding power. This does not make fake identities impossible, but forces attackers to fund every active identity and bear the cost of immobilized capital.
